record.paper: On the Complexity of Digraph Colourings and Vertex Arboricity

dossier_meta.paper: On the Complexity of Digraph Colourings and Vertex Arboricity
dossier_meta.statement_text: For given $k,b\in\mathbb{N}$ with $k\geq b$, is there a directed graph $\vec{K}(k,b)$ with vertex set $\binom{[k]}{b}$ such that the following holds? The subdigraph of $\vec{K}(k,b)$ induced by any $\{B_{1},\ldots,B_{l}\}\subseteq\binom{[k]}{b}$ is acylic if and only if $\bigcap_{i=1}^{l}{B_{i}}\neq\emptyset$.
dossier_meta.context_text: Such 'directed Kneser graphs' $\vec{K}(k,b)$ would allow $b$-tuple $k$-colourings of digraphs to be equivalent to the existence of circular homomorphisms to $\vec{K}(k,b)$, tying the fractional dichromatic number to circular homomorphism theory. Existence is confirmed for $k=b+1$ via the directed cycle of length $b+1$, but the general case is open.
